purpose: First evidence tranche for the fourteen return-panel assets that are not yet classification-verified, covering the five rule-mechanical codes whose determination is a fact check against protocol documentation.
tranche_order_rule: Tranches are ordered by evidence difficulty, fixed before estimation: A rule-mechanical codes (gas, stake, scarcity, burn, protocol), B ninety-day data-pull codes (collateral, monetary), C judgment codes (governance, utility, incentive). Codes were NOT selected by which bundle showed signal in P1_H6; selecting codes by outcome would compromise that frozen test.
coder: drafting pass by the research assistant, with source URLs spot-checked by refetching
adjudication_rule: Decisions held pending require adjudication before they may be scored. A pending cell never becomes a zero by default.

consistency_cases.question: On UTXO proof-of-work chains a zero-fee transaction is consensus-valid and fee minimums are node relay policy. The verified BTC decision scores this 0. BCH, LTC, DOGE, and ZEC share that property, so scoring them 1 would contradict the BTC precedent.
consistency_cases.recommendation: Apply the BTC precedent and score all four 0, or revise the VA_GAS rule to admit economically required fees and re-review BTC. Do not resolve the two chains differently.

consistency_cases.question: Chainlink staking rewards are currently emissions-funded, which is service compensation, but the official economics page describes a Reserve and Smart Value Recapture. Whether either mechanically terminates value at LINK has not been established from primary sources.
consistency_cases.recommendation: Obtain primary documentation of the Reserve's disposition before scoring.

independent_replication.scope: The ten burn and protocol decisions for SOL, AVAX, TRX, XRP, and ADA already carry reviewed evidence in config/crypto_h2_expansion_evidence.json and the effective-dated ledger.
independent_replication.result: All ten drafted decisions match the existing reviewed values, an independent replication of the previously adjudicated set including the Cardano governed-treasury call.

decisions.rationale: Cardano computes a deterministic protocol fee (a*size+b) in lovelace for every transaction; no alternative fee asset exists and a zero-fee transaction is not valid.
ADA is delegated to stake pools under Ouroboros and block-production probability is proportional to delegated stake, so the token secures consensus.
The mainnet Shelley genesis file hard-codes maxLovelaceSupply of 45,000,000,000,000,000 lovelace (45bn ADA), a consensus-level terminal bound changeable only by hard fork.
Fees collected in an epoch are redistributed to stake pools and delegators rather than destroyed, so no live rules-based burn exists. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.

Treasury funds are released only by discretionary governance action to grants and ecosystem work, which is VA_GOV under the governed-treasury capture boundary. Independently reproduces the existing adjudicated decision.
AVAX is the required fee asset for transactions and contract execution on the Avalanche primary network.
Validators must bond AVAX to participate in Avalanche consensus, placing the token economically at risk to secure the network.
Issuance is bounded by a protocol-enforced asymptotic maximum of 720m AVAX rather than a discretionary target.
All AVAX paid in transaction fees is permanently burned by protocol rule. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.
Fee burn is a mechanical route by which network revenue terminates at the token itself. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.

Held pending the relay-policy versus consensus-rule boundary. A zero-fee BCH transaction is consensus-valid and fee minimums are node relay policy, matching the reasoning behind the existing verified BTC VA_GAS=0 decision. Adjudication required before this cell is scored.
Bitcoin Cash is secured by SHA-256 proof of work with no staking, delegation, or locked-token risk.
The protocol enforces a 21m coin terminal supply through the halving schedule, changeable only by hard fork.
The block specification requires the coinbase transaction to collect and spend transaction fees to the miner, so fees are paid out rather than destroyed.
Fees and subsidy are paid to miners as compensation for block production, which is service payment rather than a mechanical route to holders.
Held pending the same relay-policy versus consensus-rule boundary as BTC and the other UTXO proof-of-work chains.
Dogecoin uses Scrypt proof-of-work consensus with no staking or delegation of the token.
Official documentation states that Dogecoin's issuance does not have an end date, so there is no terminal supply bound.

Dogecoin documents transaction fees as miner compensation in addition to the block subsidy. Under the existing usage-linked burn rule, this is redistribution, not a protocol fee burn. Voluntary destruction or lost keys do not establish a usage-linked mechanism.

Transaction fees and the block subsidy compensate miners for securing and producing blocks. This service payment does not route protocol revenue mechanically to DOGE holders under the strict capture rule.
HBAR is required to pay transaction, smart contract, and storage fees for all Hedera network services.
HBAR is delegated to nodes and each node's consensus influence is proportional to staked HBAR, meeting the delegation-to-secure-network test.
Total supply was fixed at 50bn HBAR at genesis with no ongoing issuance, and changing it requires unanimous Council consent.

Schedule A sections 3.1-3.2 allocate native network transaction fees to nodes and Hedera, with subsequent node payments funded by transaction fees. The documented fee route is payment and redistribution, not HBAR destruction. This concerns native HBAR, not burn operations on tokens issued through Hedera Token Service.
Fee revenue and treasury releases fund Council-directed development and ecosystem categories and node compensation, with no mechanical route terminating at the token.
LINK is an ERC-677/ERC-20 token used to pay for oracle services; it is not the fee asset of any chain it runs on, where gas is paid in the host chain's native token.
Chainlink Staking v0.2 is live and stakes LINK subject to slashing to back oracle service performance, which is protocol risk absorption.
The official economics page states total supply is capped at 1,000,000,000 LINK, created at genesis with no protocol-level minting.
The canonical economics page was refetched and describes revenue, the Reserve, Payment Abstraction, staking, and Smart Value Recapture with no token burn, so no live burn mechanism exists.

Held pending adjudication. Staking rewards are currently emissions-funded, which is service compensation, but the same page describes a Reserve and Smart Value Recapture whose relationship to the strict holder-capture rule has not been assessed from primary sources. This is the LINK analogue of the governed-treasury boundary question.
Held pending the relay-policy versus consensus-rule boundary shared with BTC, BCH, DOGE, and ZEC.
Litecoin is secured by Scrypt proof-of-work mining; the cited page describes no protocol staking or delegation of LTC.
A maximum supply of 84m LTC is enforced by a deterministic halving schedule that drives the block reward to zero around 2142.
The official FAQ explicitly allocates all fees from included transactions to miners alongside the block reward. Ordinary usage therefore pays miners rather than triggering a rules-based LTC burn.
Miners receive the block reward together with all fees in confirmed transactions, which is service payment rather than a mechanical route to LTC holders.
OP Mainnet transaction fees, including the L1 data fee, are paid in ETH rather than in OP, so OP is not the fee asset of its own chain.
Fault-proof economic security is backed by ETH-denominated bonds; OP itself is not locked or placed at risk to secure the network.
Supply inflates at a rate approved by token governance, which is an adjustable target rather than a credible terminal bound.

The buyback design sends purchased OP to the token treasury; burning is described as a possible future use, not an executed rules-based burn. Execution reports confirm treasury settlement. The optional holder burn functions in the token specification do not establish a usage-linked protocol burn. Score 0 under the existing burn rule.

Execution is established: official reports on March 5 and August 7 confirm three revenue-funded buybacks totalling 9,451,924 OP. The former statement that execution was unconfirmed is corrected. The latest report covers January-March revenue, and an August 25 question about subsequent execution is unanswered in the retrieved thread. Current active versus paused status at September 7 remains unestablished, so the live-capture value stays null; completed historical buybacks are not treated as proof of continuous operation.
Every Solana transaction requires a base fee denominated in SOL, with no alternative fee asset.
SOL is delegated to validators under proof of stake and delegated weight secures block production and voting.
Issuance disinflates toward a perpetual 1.5 percent long-term rate with no terminal cap, so the scarcity test fails.
Fifty percent of every base transaction fee is burned by protocol rule. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.
The mechanical fifty percent base-fee burn terminates value at the token. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.
SUI is the required denomination for gas fees on all Sui transactions and operations.
Validators lock SUI as collateral for the duration of an epoch under delegated proof of stake.
Total supply is capped at 10,000,000,000 SUI, with stake subsidies drawn from that fixed pool rather than open-ended issuance.
Computation fees are paid to validators and storage fees enter a storage fund, so gas revenue is redistributed rather than destroyed.
Fee revenue compensates validators and funds future storage costs, with no burn, buyback, or enforceable holder claim.
Beyond free and staked resource allowances the protocol mandatorily deducts TRX at fixed rates to pay for bandwidth and energy, so TRX is required to transact.
TRX must be staked to obtain bandwidth and energy and to vote for Super Representatives, linking locked TRX to consensus participation.
Official documentation states the total supply is not fixed, with ongoing minting offset by burning and no terminal cap.
A live rules-based burn destroys TRX at fixed rates for every resource-consuming transaction beyond allowances. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.

The live fee burn permanently removes TRX from supply, terminating value at the token; inflationary block and voter rewards are excluded as service compensation. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.
Every Stellar transaction must pay a base fee in stroops, the smallest unit of XLM, to be included in the ledger.
The Stellar Consensus Protocol selects validators through quorum and trust sets with no bonding, slashing, or economic stake at risk.
All XLM that will ever exist was created when the network went live, and the 1 percent annual inflation was ended by validator vote on 28 October 2019.
Collected fees move into a locked network account and are not given to or used by anyone, which is sequestration rather than irreversible destruction.
Fees are locked away rather than burned or distributed, so no mechanical route returns network revenue to XLM or its holders.
Every XRP Ledger transaction must destroy a small amount of XRP as its transaction cost, making the token protocol-required to transact.
XRPL consensus relies on trusted validator lists chosen by reputation, with no bonding, locking, or slashing of XRP.
All 100bn XRP were created at genesis and the protocol permits no new issuance.
The transaction cost is not paid to any party and the XRP is irrevocably destroyed. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.
Irreversible destruction of the transaction cost is a mechanical route by which network usage terminates value at the token. Independently reproduces the existing reviewed ledger decision.
Held pending the relay-policy versus consensus-rule boundary shared with the other UTXO proof-of-work chains.
Zcash is secured by Equihash proof-of-work mining, with miners earning block rewards and fees rather than any token being staked.
Zcash enforces a 21m ZEC terminal supply cap at the consensus layer.
ZIP-1014 implements the fund flow by sending newly issued block subsidy to designated addresses; no consensus rule destroys ZEC.
The development fund routes newly issued subsidy to development organizations rather than mechanically to the token or its holders, which is the same boundary applied to governed treasuries.

revision_note: Evidence review on 2026-09-14 for the existing 2026-09-07 classification. Retrieval dates are not mechanism activation dates. Five documentation gaps resolved; no historical panel or frozen experiment input changed.
